svg.aria-label: How to write 眼: 11 strokes · 10 pen lifts · 11 movements
svg.title: Writing 眼
svg.desc: 11 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 眼 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 眼.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E7%9C%BC.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 眼, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw 目 as 想 writes it: its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, two horizontals inside, then the horizontal that closes the foot. Medians 6–11 draw the right side: a horizontal that turns down without lifting, two horizontals, a vertical down the left side that turns up to the right without lifting, a short left-falling stroke, then a long right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
